definitions.gloss: unable to read the room, socially oblivious
definitions.explanation: A slang abbreviation for {空気|くうき}が{読|よ}めない (kuuki ga yomenai - can't read the atmosphere). Describes someone who fails to pick up on social cues or says inappropriate things in a given situation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧KY⟦だから→だから：00924_dakara⟧⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{壊|こわ}す→壊す：01241_kowasu⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: He can't read the room, so he sometimes ruins the atmosphere.

examples.japanese: KYな⟦{発言|はつげん}→発言：05099_hatsugen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{凍|こお}った→凍る：02100_kooru⟧。
examples.english: The room went silent after that socially oblivious comment.

examples.japanese: 「KY」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦いう→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧2000⟦{年代|ねんだい}→年代：03533_nendai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{流行|りゅうこう}→流行：03678_ryuukou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The term 'KY' became popular in the 2000s.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: Abbreviation of ⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧ (K) + ⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧ (Y), meaning "can't read the air/atmosphere." The term became widely popular around 2007 and was a top buzzword in Japan that year.

REGISTER: Casual/Slang
Primarily used in casual conversation. The abbreviation style reflects Japanese youth culture's tendency to create alphabet-based slang.

USAGE AS NA-ADJECTIVE:
・KYな⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a person who can't read the room)
・KYな⟦{発言|はつげん}→発言：05099_hatsugen⟧ (a socially oblivious remark)
・KYな⟦{行動|こうどう}→行動：02728_koudou⟧ (oblivious behavior)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・⟦{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む→空気を読む：06306_kuukiwoyomu⟧ (to read the room - positive ability)
・⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧ (can't read the room - full form)
・⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧ (the atmosphere of a place/situation)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The concept of ⟦{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む→空気を読む：06306_kuukiwoyomu⟧ reflects the importance of nonverbal communication and social harmony in Japanese culture. Being unable to do so (KY) is seen as a significant social deficiency.
